title: Responses compatibility telemetry, degradation signaling, and orchestration playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: When customers migrate workloads that expect OpenAI's Responses semantics to Redwood's Responses API, subtle mismatches in streaming events, function/tool calling handoffs, and structured-output markers cause silent degradation in UX or routing loops. We lack an authoritative telemetry surface and a runbook that both detects these degradations early and orchestrates graceful fallbacks (e.g., swap to a compatibility shim, enable lossiness-tolerant mode, or route to hosted/OpenAI-backed bridge).

Goal: Produce a telemetry schema, detection heuristics, and an automated orchestration playbook to: 1) surface parity regressions in streaming/function-calling/structured output, 2) emit deterministic signals for routing/fallback decisions, and 3) implement an incremental rollout strategy for the compatibility shim with observable rollback criteria.

Scope: This ticket covers schema design, signal thresholds, an initial set of detectors for streaming/func-call/structured-output mismatches, a runtime flagging API for the router, and a canary orchestration plan. Implementation tasks are limited to instrumentation + pipeline config and a lightweight orchestrator that triggers one of three mitigation actions. Integration with full shim logic is tracked in dependent tickets.

Out of scope: full-feature parity fixes inside the model runtime or long-lived protocol translation proxy (these are separate epics).
acceptance_criteria: Schema defined and reviewed: telemetry events + attributes necessary to diagnose streaming, toolcall, and structured output gaps
Detectors: three rule-based detectors implemented in telemetry pipeline (streaming truncation, toolcall handshake mismatch, structured-JSON-escape anomalies)
Router API: runtime signal endpoint that accepts a degradation token and recommended mitigation (shim|lossy-mode|route-openai)
Orchestration runbook: documented canary plan (1%, 10%, 100%), automated rollback triggers based on error/latency/regression metrics
Dashboards: a new dashboard tile in Console showing parity score, active mitigations, and incident timeline
Tests: unit tests for detectors and an integration test that simulates a parity regression and verifies orchestrator action
tasks: Design telemetry schema (events: resp.stream_chunk, resp.func_call.start/complete, resp.structured.output) - owner Maya
Implement detectors in kinesis->flink job and add alert rules - owner Liam
Expose runtime routing API to accept degradation tokens - owner Infra (Brad Wong)
Create Console dashboard prototype and link to ticket - owner Product (Sofia Ruiz)
Write canary orchestration script with 3-step rollout and rollback conditions - owner SRE (Hannah Lee)
Coordinate dry-run with Solutions Eng and 2 pilot customers (internal opt-in) - owner SE (Alex Gomez)
risks_and_tradeoffs: False positives: aggressive detectors may trigger unnecessary fallbacks, increasing cost and confusing customers
Visibility gap: some compatibility failures only surface in very long-tail prompts; detectors may need adaptive sampling
Latency vs fidelity: fallback to shim introduces latency and might change token pricing characteristics; orchestration must balance UX vs cost
Complexity: adding another routing signal increases runtime decision surface and testing burden
design_decisions: Use discrete degradation tokens (enum) rather than free-form messages to keep router logic simple: {NO_ACTION, SHIM, LOSSY_MODE, ROUTE_OPENAI}
Start with rule-based detectors (deterministic heuristics) and instrument scoring buckets to evaluate need for ML-driven detectors later
Emit parity_score as a single 0-100 metric aggregated per-route to simplify dashboarding and SLIs
Canary rollout windows: 30m warmup, 3h watch, 24h stability before wider expansion
